images.filename: Forest Heritage National Scenic Byway - Pisgah National Forest Entrance Arch - NARA - 7718480.jpg
images.caption:
Scope and content:  The original finding aid described this photograph as:
Original Caption: This historical image shows the entrance arch into Pisgah National Forest as it appeared from 1916 to 1936, until U.S. 276 was built. A historic black car can be seen driving under the columned archway that bears the words "Pisgah National Forest."
Location: Location: Pisgah National Forest, North Carolina (35.274° N 82.707° W)

Status: Public domain.

images.caption:
A Forest Service life guard jumps into the cold waters of Sliding Rock to help out a patron in the Pisgah National Forest, NC. 
Sliding Rock is a 60-foot slippery cascade into the 50-60 degree, 7-foot deep pool. There are 2 observation platforms, and lifeguards on duty during the season. This is a heavily used recreation area which often fills to capacity. Persons parking on the side of the road, outside of the designated parking area, will be ticketed. It is suggested, too, that you wear old shorts and old sneakers if you choose to take the plunge. Entry is $2.00 per person for sliders and observers. (Forest Service photo by Cecilio Ricardo)
